memory_raw.text: Taric gathers Esa to talk.

Beyond this season is exactly what worries me — I'm forty-seven with one food and no one who shares my blood, and if this year goes bad I've got no one to fall back on. What I'm thinking is that you and I stop being two people who are friendly and start being two people who are genuinely bound — but that takes more than goodwill, it takes a reason neither of us would walk away from.
Taric gathers Esa to talk.

A child would do it — yours and mine, something we'd both have cause to protect. I know you're forty-four and the window's narrow, but it's still open, and three food between us buys more than another year of watching each other's backs from a distance.
Taric cannot offer a child to Esa: Taric cannot spare the 2 food they offered (holds 1).
Taric gathers Esa to talk.

I hear you, and I won't pretend the idea doesn't pull at me — but three food between us means one of us eats thin this year and we start the next season already behind, with a child depending on us and Dav's household sitting fat. Give me something first: a share of your food now, something that shows you mean this as a real binding and not just words when you're scared.
Taric gathers Esa to talk.

You want proof before you risk anything — fine, that's honest, and I respect it more than easy agreement. But I'm the one sitting on one food, Esa; if I give you something now I'm the one who starves if the year turns, and that doesn't make me a bound partner, it makes me desperate. Tell me what you need from me that doesn't cost me the only margin I have.
Esa gives 1 food to Taric.

Bram, after what you pulled on Roan last year I wasn't sure I'd be speaking to you privately — but the pile's gone and neither of us got a piece of it, and I'd rather have that conversation now than after someone else decides our food is easier to take than theirs.

Bram, I'll say it straight: Vela walked away with five food this year and Dav's household is fat while you and I are standing here with nothing from the pile — whatever bad blood there was, that's a bigger problem than the two of us right now. Taric, you're the one I trust in this room, so I want your read before I say more: are you and Bram solid, or am I making this offer to the wrong man?
Dav gives 1 food to Ryn.
Dell gives 1 food to Dav.
Esa gathers Bram, Taric to talk.

Taric hasn't answered and I'm not going to wait on it — Bram, you've got six food and strength enough to matter, and I've got one food and a promise I'm trying to build into something real before the year turns hard. What I want to know is whether Roan's still a grudge or whether that's done, because if it's done, you and I have something to talk about.
Taric gives 1 food to Esa.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Pile's gone before half of us got near it — Vela took five, Dav took two and fed Ryn three more, and Mako walked away with two more on top of whatever he's still sitting on from last year. I'm at zero food and I need to know who in this room can spare one before the year closes, because a man who can't eat doesn't defend anyone. What are we each holding?

I've got two food and I'll give you one, Kael — a man at zero is a liability to himself and everyone standing near him, and I'd rather spend one now than watch you fold when it counts. But I want to know what happened at the pile, because I didn't get there in time and five to Vela in two pulls is something we should have stopped before it finished.

Esa, take the food back — I'll name what happened at the pile myself: I was late, same as you, and by the time I got there the quick hands had already cleared it. Vela, I'm not accusing you in front of this room, but five in two pulls when the pile only had fifteen for twelve people is a number that needs explaining, because the rest of us are doing sums and coming up short.

Vela, I've got no quarrel with a person feeding themselves, but five out of fifteen when half the room went empty is the kind of thing that makes people start counting who owes what — so I'd rather hear your reason now, in this room, than find out later you had one and didn't offer it.

Vela, we're all listening and the room's not hostile — but silence right now looks worse than whatever the honest answer is, so give it to us plain and let us move on to the part where we figure out how nobody starves before the year closes.

Vela, I've spoken twice and Kael's spoken twice and you've said nothing, which is itself an answer — so I'll stop waiting and say what the room is already thinking: eight food on a woman of forty-eight while Kael sits at zero is a stockpile, not a meal, and stockpiles invite counting. If you've got a reason we should feel good about that number, now's the last easy moment to give it.

Vela, I'll ask it one final time because I've known you three years and I'd rather not draw the wrong conclusion — either you say what you took so much for, or this circle starts treating your eight food the way we'd treat Mako's seven, and you know what that means for how safe you sleep.

Pile's gone before I got near it — I'm holding one food and the year just started. Mako walked away with the most again and now he's given something to Sela, which means either he's generous or he's buying something, and I don't think he's generous. I need one of you to give me food to see the year out, and I'll owe that debt when it matters.

memory_summary:
In year one Taric pulled me and Ryn into a quiet pact — two each from the pile, watch each other's backs — and that felt like the first real thing in this village. Kael's circle followed: me, Sela, Vela, Ryn, all swearing to bleed together, though Ryn dragged her feet and Dav's name hung in the air the whole time. Then Ryn had Dav's child and I felt the circle shift — she didn't leave us, but she stopped being fully ours.

Taric is the one I trust. He gave me food when I was thin and named me plainly as the person he counts on — I've given back twice now, so the debt runs both ways, which is how I want it. His talk of a child stings a little; the window on my side is closed and we both know it, but he still chose me to stand with, and that's not nothing.

Bram tried to take Roan and the whole village stood against him until he backed down. I was in that line. He hasn't forgiven it, and I haven't forgotten that he tried.

Vela fed Bram three times out of a circle that swore to stand together — that's a quiet betrayal I've noted and haven't named to her face yet. Mako's been fat and silent for four years running, and silence on a man that strong is the thing that frightens me most.
name: Esa
